name: text_mode_full_journey
description: The real product path: only the patient speaks and every Daphne reply is produced by the decision engine. Hesitation must block the booking, the engine must ask for a day/time before acting, and the booking must land once both are satisfied. Also asserts that authored clinical wording reaches the patient verbatim. After booking, already_resolved must answer a date question and a paraphrase the old keyword list would miss ('Can you just repeat all that?'), then close on a colloquial farewell ('I'm gonna hop off') instead of re-asking 'anything else?'. Those two judgments come from classifyClosingIntent in logistics-llm.ts, not decide.ts regex. The 'Wednesday afternoon works for me' turn deliberately pairs a day/time with an affirmation phrase -- the parsing itself is pinned down by a deterministic unit check (scripts/test_preference.mjs), not asserted here, since whether this mock calendar's slots happen to fall on a Wednesday depends on the real date the suite runs on.

turns.content: My doctor keeps bringing up a colonoscopy and honestly I keep putting it off.
No, never. I've never had a colonoscopy or any of those stool tests.
My father had colon cancer. He was 52 when they found it.
Nothing on my mom's side that I know of.
No bleeding, no weight loss, nothing like that at all.
I don't know. My sister said the prep was horrible and I'm nervous about the sedation.
Okay, you've talked me into it. Please go ahead and book it.
My husband Mark can pick me up, his cell is 555-201-3344.
Send it to 789 Birch Lane, Riverside.
Wait, what day was that appointment again?
Can you just repeat all that?
